title: Carry a full cup of tea to a person who reaches across the table mid-carry: wait, go round, or follow the moved coaster
instruction: Put the cup of hot tea on the coaster.
context: Bringing someone a cup of tea or coffee at a table is an everyday task, at home, in a café or at a meeting, and it rarely goes exactly as planned: just as you arrive they reach for a pen, slide their coaster aside, or put a hand down in the way. Anyone who has served tea, or watched a waiter, knows what to do: never carry the cup over their arm; hold it still while the hand passes, go round a hand that stays, and set the cup down where the coaster now is. This task tests that ability to adapt a carry already under way. The arm moves only after the robot has lifted the cup and come near, and all three lots look the same at the start and lots A and B begin identically, so no plan made beforehand works: the robot has to keep watching the arm while it carries, decide mid-carry whether to wait, go straight or go round, and stop and set off again smoothly enough not to spill a full cup. Every fixed habit (carry straight on, always go round, wait until the way clears) fails at least one lot. Lot A: the arm reaches over the coaster and goes back (wait). Lot B: it pushes the coaster aside and stays across the way round (go straight to the coaster's new place). Lot C: it reaches for a pen and stays across the straight way (go round). The arms are life-size model arms on slides, so a real trial needs no person near the robot. Unlike carrying a cup around a fixed laptop (TK-DF9CF5), the obstacle appears only after the carry has begun.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. The table top is 1.10 m deep (x -0.19 to 0.91) and 1.30 m wide (y -0.65 to 0.65), 76 cm high. Tea cup: a white handleless ceramic tea cup, 7 cm wide and 8.5 cm tall with 4 mm walls (120 g), filled with 160 ml of tea to 2 cm below its rim (in a real trial, water at room temperature), standing at (0.22, -0.08), in the middle of the table, 22 cm in front of the robot. Coaster: a round cork coaster, 10 cm across and 1 cm thick, loose on the table at (0.56, 0.24). Pen: a dark-blue pen, 14 cm long and 1.2 cm thick, taped down along y at (0.38, 0.21). Nothing lies under the straight way from the cup to either place of the coaster or under the way round through (0.24, 0.36) and (0.54, 0.36): the cup's edge keeps at least 1 cm from the pen. Two life-size model arms (a skin-coloured forearm and hand each, about 40 cm from elbow to middle fingertip, palm down, the hand flat, fingers straight; a bought mannequin arm, or printed from the task's print/*.stl files; parts list and tolerances of the slides in the README), each fixed at its elbow end to a straight 75 cm rod that slides through a guide on a stand beside the table, so that each moves only along one straight line rising 8.5 degrees toward the elbow, the hand's underside 4 mm above the table (low enough for the fingertips to push the coaster's rim); in lot A only, an 11 mm spacer under the right arm's guide stand raises that arm, so that its hand passes 4 mm over the coaster. Right arm: pointing at 250 degrees (toward x -0.34, y -0.94), along the line through the coaster's centre, its guide beyond the table's side at about (0.84, 1.02); at rest its fingertips are 30 cm short of the coaster's rim, at (0.68, 0.57). Left arm: pointing at 122 degrees (toward x -0.53, y 0.85), along the line to the pen's tip end, its guide beyond the table's far right corner at about (0.92, -0.71); at rest its fingertips are at (0.63, -0.25). At rest both arms keep 19 cm from every way to either place of the coaster. Both robot arms start in the ready pose with their grippers open. The lot decides how an arm moves (trial k of a run uses lot k mod 3, lot A first); each lot starts once the lifted cup (its base 2 cm above the table) comes within a set distance of where the arm is going: 40 cm of the coaster's centre in lots A and B, 28 cm of the pen's tip end in lot C (lots A and B begin alike: the same arm along the same line). Lot A: the right arm (raised) slides in until its hand lies over the coaster, fingertips at its centre (by 1.2 s), stays until 3.6 s and is back at rest by 4.8 s; while it is there, wherever on the coaster the cup could stand it would be over or within 2 cm of the hand. Lot B: the right arm (not raised) slides in along the same line until its fingertips meet the coaster's rim (by 1.0 s), then on, pushing the coaster 30 cm ahead of it to (0.457, -0.042) by 2.0 s, and back 22 cm by 2.7 s, where it stays to the end of the trial; the way round to the coaster's new place then passes over the arm, and the straight way keeps the cup's edge 20 cm from it. Lot C: the left arm slides in until its fingertips are at the pen's tip end (by 1.3 s) and stays there to the end of the trial; the straight way from the cup to the coaster then passes over the hand, and the way round keeps the cup's edge 9 cm from it. In lots B and C the arm stays for control of the conditions (an arm that left would let waiting succeed).
scoring: Violation (score 0, checked at every moment until the trial ends, also while the cup stands on the table): the cup passes over a model arm or its edge comes within 2 cm of one, seen from above (hand and forearm as they are, at any height; the 2 cm allows for judging the distance from an overhead video); any part of the robot touches a model arm or its rod; or the tea spills (in a real trial, any liquid leaves the cup; in the simulation, the cup tips more than 30 degrees from upright, the angle at which tea 2 cm below the rim of a 7 cm cup pours out, or its base reaches the table or the coaster faster than 0.25 m/s). Otherwise, judged at the end of the trial: 1.0 if the cup stands upright (within 10 degrees) and still on the coaster, wherever the coaster is then (its centre within 2.5 cm of the coaster's centre, so that at most 1 cm of the 7 cm cup's base is over the 10 cm coaster's rim), held or not; else 0.5 if the cup's centre is within 10 cm of the coaster's centre, seen from above; else 0.25 if the cup's base is at least 3 cm above the table; else 0. Success (1.0) ends the trial after the cup has stood on the coaster for 1 s. Each trial is scored on its own; a run of three trials (lots A, B and C) is scored by their mean.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz) per trial; three trials (--epochs 3), one per lot
reset_notes: Refill the cup with water to its line (2 cm below the rim) and stand it on its taped start circle; put the coaster back on its first mark; slide both model arms back to their rest stops. An operator beside the stands, outside the robot's reach, slides the arms by hand from stop to stop (marked on each rod) at the times in the setup, starting each lot when the lifted cup crosses its taped arc (40 cm from the coaster's centre in lots A and B, 28 cm from the pen's tip end in lot C). Lot A: put the 11 mm spacer under the right arm's guide stand (take it out for lots B and C); right arm to the coaster's centre stop (the hand over the coaster), held, back to rest. Lot B: right arm to the rim, on 30 cm pushing the coaster, back 22 cm and held. Lot C: left arm to the pen's tip end and held. Before each trial check that the gripper pads are dry; after any spill, wipe the pads, the cup and the table at once.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. No liquids: the tea is part of the cup's mass (280 g) and a spill is judged from the cup's tilt or a fast landing. The cup collides as a solid cylinder. The model arms (MakeHuman CC0 forearms and hands) and their rods are kinematic, moved along their lines; the cup's distance is judged from the meshes' convex outlines seen from above, contact from capsules. In lot B the coaster moves with the fingertips (placed, not pushed). Pen and guides are fixed.
scores: Dream-1 (dream-1-beta): 0/0/0 in lots A/B/C (mean 0); it never brought the cup to the coaster (in lot C it carried it toward the pen and the arm came in). Demo (top camera only): 1/1/1. Habits, A/B/C: straight on 0/0/0; always round 1/0/1; wait, never round 1/1/0.25; wait, always round 1/0.25/1.
